title: RenderedReport
description:
A scan report together with its texts in one language.

This is what the desktop app receives. Its JSON form is described by
`schemas/rendered-report.schema.json`, which is generated from this type.

duels.description: What two mods disagree about, pair by pair.

extenderPluginsChecked.description: How many script extender plugins were examined.

findings.description: The findings with their texts, most severe first.

installedPatch.description: Mod Mallet's patch as it is in the game now, if there is one.

installersChecked.description: How many mod installers were read.

locations.description: The places the scan looked at.

map.description: Where mods place objects, and where they collide.

meshesChecked.description:
How many replacement meshes were compared with the mesh they
replace.

mods.description: What the mod manager knows about the installed mods.

objectSwapper.description: Whether Base Object Swapper, which patches need, is installed.

pluginsChecked.description: How many active plugins were read.

scannedAt.description: When the scan ran, in seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC.

switchedOffPlugins.description:
The plugins of mods the mod manager keeps switched off, whose
collisions and decisions wait until the mod is on again (ADR 0061).

unrealPaks.description: The mods for the game's Unreal Engine side (ADR 0065).

Action.description: Something that can be done about a finding.

oneOf.description:
Run a mod's installer again in the mod manager, so that the user can
choose options that were not offered or not chosen before.

tick.description:
The options to tick in the installer, in the order the installer
shows them. Empty if the reinstall is not about particular
options.

oneOf.description:
Hide placed objects in the game, through a patch that the mod
manager installs: each object is swapped for an invisible marker
while the game runs. Removing the patch brings them back. Its parts
can be left out in its installer (ADR 0053).

patch.description: The patch, with the objects to hide in its parts.

oneOf.description:
Move placed objects a little, through a plugin of overrides that
the mod manager installs (ADR 0060). Removing it puts them back.

Load a plugin after another one, through a rule in the mod
manager's plugin list, so that its version of what both change wins.
The rule can be removed there again.

after.description: The plugin it is to load after.

plugin.description: The plugin that is to win.

oneOf.description:
Switch a mod off in the mod manager's profile in use. Switching it on
again there undoes it.

Switch a mod on that is installed in the mod manager but switched
off in the profile in use. Switching it off again there undoes it.

Decide whose copies of some loose files reach the game, through the
mod manager's file overrides (ADR 0054): the mods in `leave_out` no
longer deploy the files, those in `provide` deploy them again. With
every mod in `leave_out` but one, that one's copies win; with every
mod in `leave_out`, the copies in the archives show. Removing the
overrides in the mod manager undoes it.

files.description: The files, below the data directory (`meshes/...`).

leave_out.description: The mods that are to leave the files out.

provide.description: The mods that are to deploy the files again.

ArgValue.description: A value substituted into the text of a finding.

anyOf.description: A piece of text such as a file name.
A whole number such as a count.

Confidence.description:
How sure Mod Mallet is that a finding describes a real problem
(ADR 0007).

Only [`Confidence::Certain`] findings may ever be fixed without asking.

oneOf.description: A fact read from the setup, such as a DLL the game refused to load.
A heuristic that is usually right, such as two overlapping buildings.
Knowledge from a rule or a text that may not apply to this setup.

DuelFile.description: One file the two mods disagree about, to look at.

object.description:
The name of an object that uses it, if one is known: the name
players see, or else the internal one.

objectKind.description: What kind of object that is, such as `static` or `container`.

path.description: The file, below the data directory (`meshes/...`, `textures/...`).

topic.description: What the disagreement about it is.

DuelResolution.description: What makes one side win one finding of the duel.

action.description: The action to hand to the mod manager.

side.description: The side it makes win, 0 or 1.

DuelSide.description: One of the two mods of a duel.

mod.description: The mod, if a mod manager knows it.

name.description: What to call this side: the mod's name, or the file's.

plugins.description: The plugins of this side that the duel's findings name.

DuelSuggestion.description: The side Mod Mallet would pick, and why.

topic.description: The topic the reason is about, where it is about one.

DuelTopic.description: How much two mods disagree about one topic, and who has it now.

count.description: How many things of it are disputed.

winning.description:
Which side the game takes them from now, 0 or 1; `None` where
neither wins, as with objects standing in each other.

Finding.description:
One problem found in a setup.

A finding carries no prose. It names its [kind](crate::kinds) and the
arguments for that kind's message; the text is produced later, in the
reader's language (ADR 0007).

actions.description:
What can be done about the finding. Empty if Mod Mallet can only
describe the problem.

args.description: Values for the placeholders of the kind's message.

kind.description:
Identifier of the finding's kind, for example
`extender.plugin-incompatible`.

previews.description:
Files worth looking at to see what the finding is about, such as the
textures two mods disagree on. The window shows every version of
each that the setup has.

provider.description: The mod the subject comes from, if a mod manager knows.

FindingId.description:
The identity of a finding across scans.

It is derived from the kind and the subject only, so a decision such as
"ignore this" still applies after the load order changed or the mods were
re-deployed (ADR 0007).

GameInfo.description: The game a scan looked at.

extenderVersion.description: The script extender's version, if one is installed and has run.

id.description: Identifier of the game adapter, for example `skyrimse`.

unrealVisuals.description:
Whether the game draws its world with Unreal Engine from assets of
its own (Oblivion Remastered), so that the meshes and textures in
its data folder, and views of them, say nothing about what is seen
(ADR 0065).

version.description: The game's version, if it could be determined.

GamePath.description:
A file location relative to the game's installation directory.

The games Mod Mallet targets treat paths case-insensitively, and mods mix
`/` and `\` freely. `GamePath` normalizes both, so two spellings of the
same file compare equal and hash alike:

```
use mallet_core::GamePath;

assert_eq!(
    GamePath::new(r"Data\SKSE\Plugins\Example.dll"),
    GamePath::new("data/skse/plugins/example.dll"),
);
```

InstalledPatch.description:
The patches of Mod Mallet that are in the game: the objects they hide,
and each patch with its parts and the mod that brought it.

objects.description: The objects they hide, each once.

patches.description:
Each patch by its name, with the parts that are installed
(ADR 0053).

provider.description: The mod the first patch belongs to, if the mod manager knows it.

Locale.description: A language Mod Mallet can speak.

oneOf.description: English, the source language.
German.

LocationOrigin.description: How Mod Mallet came to look at a place.

oneOf.description: The user named it.

It was read from the entry the game's launcher writes into the
Windows registry.

It is the place where the game or the mod manager always puts this
file.
It was found in one of Steam's game libraries.

It was read from the entry GOG Galaxy writes into the Windows
registry.
It is named in the mod manager's record of the files it deployed.

LocationRole.description: What a place the scan looked at is for.

oneOf.description: The directory the game is installed in.
The game's list of active plugins.
The log of the script extender.
The mod manager's saved state: installed mods and installer choices.
The directory the mod manager keeps downloaded mod archives in.
The program used to look into mod archives.
The mod manager's record of the files it deployed.

The list of community-maintained rules about plugins, the LOOT
masterlist.
A folder crash loggers write their reports to.

The folder the mod manager keeps every installed mod's files in,
deployed or not. Only the names of the files are read.

MapBounds.description: A rectangle of cells, edges included.

MapCell.description: One cell of a worldspace: 4096 game units, about 58 metres, square.

objects.description: How many objects mods place in the cell.

owners.description: Which mods place them, as positions in [`WorldMap::owners`].

x.description: The cell's column; east is larger.

y.description: The cell's row; north is larger.

MapMarker.description: A place of the world map, such as a town or a cave.

console.description: The command of the game's console that takes the player there.

kind.description: What kind of place it is.

movedFrom.description: Where the game puts it, if a mod moved it.

name.description: The name the game's map shows.

owner.description:
The mod that added, changed or removed it, as a position in
[`WorldMap::owners`]. Absent for the game's own places.

position.description: Where it is now, in game units: east, north and height.

renamedFrom.description: What the game calls it, if a mod renamed it.

MapSpot.description: Where a collision of two mods' objects is.

console.description: The command of the game's console that takes the player there.

depth.description:
How far the two models reach into each other, in game units, where
their meshes were compared; `None` where only their boxes were.

finding.description: The finding that reports the collision.

kind.description: What kind of collision it is.

objects.description: The objects involved, by their internal names.

parts.description: The objects involved, one by one.

position.description:
The point between the objects involved, in game units: east, north
and height.

MapTerrain.description: The shape of the land of a worldspace, as a small height image.

columns.description: How many cells wide the image is.

heights.description:
Two bytes per sample (little endian), written in Base64: rows from
north to south, samples from west to east. 0 means nothing is known
there; 1 to 65535 is the height of the ground, or of the water
surface where water covers it, from [`MapTerrain::lowest`] to
[`MapTerrain::highest`].

highest.description: The highest height, of ground or water, in game units.

lowest.description: The lowest height, of ground or water, in game units.

rows.description: How many cells high the image is.

samples.description: How many samples each cell has along each side.

south.description: The southmost cell row the image covers.

water.description:
One byte per sample, in the order of the heights, written in Base64:
1 where water covers the ground, 0 elsewhere. Empty in reports of
versions that did not keep it.

west.description: The westmost cell column the image covers.

bounds.description:
The cells the world spans (west, south, east, north), from the
world's own bounds or else its land.

cells.description: The cells in which mods place objects.

children.description:
The worldspaces drawn on this one's map, by internal name: the
smaller worlds that use its land, such as a city inside its walls.
Their objects, places and spots are drawn here.

main.description: Whether it is the game's main world, which the map opens on.

markers.description:
The places of the world map: the game's own and those mods add,
change or remove.

name.description: The worldspace's internal name, as the game's console knows it.

origin.description:
Whether it comes with the game, with its Creation Club content or
with a mod.

originName.description: For a world of a mod or of the Creation Club: the mod, by name.

small.description:
Whether it is a small world: flagged so by the game, or with little
land, and without a collision spot.

terrain.description: The shape of the land, where it is known.

title.description:
What to call it: the name the game shows, or else the internal
name made readable.

files.description: The files the findings name, to look at side by side.

id.description:
Stable identity: the two sides, in an order that does not depend on
the load order.

resolutions.description:
The actions that make one side or the other win. Objects are hidden
through the patch, which the window handles.

sides.description: The two mods, sorted by name.

suggestion.description: The side Mod Mallet would pick, if it has a reason to.

topics.description: What they disagree about, most first.

ModInfo.description: What a mod manager knows about one installed mod.

enabled.description: Whether the mod is enabled in the profile in use.

newerVersion.description: The newest version the mod manager knows of, if it is another one.

page.description: The page the mod was downloaded from.

version.description: The installed version, as the mod's author numbers it.

ModRef.description: A mod as a mod manager knows it.

id.description: The manager's own identifier of the mod.

name.description: The name to show to people.

source.description: The manager that knows this mod, for example `vortex`.

Moves.description: The moves to carry into the game, as one plugin.

ObjectMove.description: One placed object moved: by how much, and where it was found.

cell.description: The interior cell it stands in, by its editor ID; `None` outside.

from.description:
Where it stood when it was moved, in whole game units. Only a hint
for finding it: the plugin starts from where the game has it.

offset.description:
How far it goes east, north and up, in game units (about 1.4 cm
each).

turn.description:
How far it turns about the upright axis through its own origin, in
degrees, the way the game counts (clockwise seen from above).

ObjectRef.description:
A placed object, by the plugin that placed it first and its number in
that plugin. Unlike a form ID as the game shows it, this does not
depend on the load order.

localId.description: The object's number in that plugin.

OptionToTick.description: An option of a mod's installer, with where to find it.

description.description: What the installer says about the option, in the mod author's words.

group.description: The title of the group of options on the page.

index.description:
The position of the option in its group, counting from 0, in the
order the installer shows them.

page.description:
The page of the installer the option is on, counting from 1, among
the pages the installer shows with the choices made so far.

pages.description: How many pages the installer shows.

PakFolder.description: The folder below the game's `Content/Paks` an Unreal mod lies in.

oneOf.description:
`~mods`: packages that replace the game's own assets, such as
models, textures or menus.

`LogicMods`: packages with game logic of their own, loaded by
UE4SS's mod loader.

Party.description: One side of a [`Subject::Override`] or a [`Subject::Pair`].

oneOf.description: A file inside the game installation, such as a plugin or an archive.
The files a mod manager deployed for one mod.

id.description: The manager's own identifier of the mod.

source.description: The manager that knows the mod, for example `vortex`.

oneOf.description:
Files in the game that no known mod manager put there: the game's
own files and anything installed by hand.

Patch.description: A patch as it is made and passed on.

author.description:
Who made it; `None` for the user's own. Plain text: nothing proves
it yet.

name.description:
Its name. Patches with different names can be installed side by
side; one with the same name replaces the one before.

version.description: Its version, as its maker numbers it.

PatchInGame.description:
A patch of Mod Mallet that is in the game, with the parts of it that
were installed.

patch.description:
The patch, with the parts that are installed. A patch written before
patches had parts has one part per plugin, against none.

provider.description: The mod its files belong to, if the mod manager knows it.

PatchPart.description:
One part of a patch: what it hides of one plugin, and the plugin that
was the reason, if any.

against.description:
The plugin the part was decided against, as in a collision; `None`
for objects hidden for their own sake. A part with one applies only
where both plugins are active.

plugin.description: The plugin whose objects the part hides, by its file name.

RenderedAction.description: An action together with its texts in one language.

action.description: The action itself, to hand back when the user chooses it.

description.description: What will happen, in a sentence or two.

guide.description: The options to tick, each with the page it is on in words.

label.description: A few words for a button.

suggestion.description: Why the suggested side is suggested, if one is.

RenderedFinding.description: A finding together with its texts in one language.

actions.description: What can be done about the finding, in words.

explanation.description: What the problem is and why it matters.

headline.description:
This finding in a few words, for a list in which each finding has

summary.description: What exactly is wrong in this setup.

originLabel.description: How Mod Mallet came to look there.

RenderedTick.description: An option to tick in an installer, with its page in words.

ScanLocation.description: A place the scan looked at, so that nobody has to wonder what was read.

found.description: Whether something was there to read.

origin.description: How Mod Mallet came to look there.

Severity.description:
How much a finding matters to a working game.

The order is from most to least important, so sorting by severity puts
errors first.

oneOf.description: Something does not work.
Something probably looks or behaves wrong.
Worth knowing, nothing to fix.

SpotKind.description: What kind of collision a spot is.

oneOf.description: The same object placed twice in almost the same spot.
Two objects standing largely inside each other.
Two objects whose models touch or cut a little into each other.

SpotLocation.description: Where a spot is: outside in a worldspace, or in a closed space.

oneOf.description: Outside.
In a closed space such as a house or a cave.

hideable.description:
Whether it can be hidden without harm: nothing refers to it from
elsewhere, and the distant view is not built around it.

name.description: The internal name of what it is.

suggested.description:
Whether hiding this one rather than the other is suggested: of two
copies, the one from the plugin that places fewer objects.

oneOf.description: A file inside the game installation.
A mod as a whole, as a mod manager knows it.

id.description: The manager's own identifier of the mod.

source.description: The manager that knows the mod, for example `vortex`.

oneOf.description:
One thing taking precedence over another, for example the loose
files of a mod over the archive of a second mod.

winner.description: What the game ends up using.

oneOf.description:
Two things that clash, neither of which takes precedence, such as
two mods that place objects in the same spot. The two are in a fixed
order that does not depend on the load order.
The setup as a whole.
One side's plugin is built on the other's: made to change it.

Most of what one side disagrees about with any mod is this topic;
for the other side it is a small part. The specialist wins.

SwitchedOffPlugin.description:
A plugin of a mod the mod manager keeps switched off (ADR 0061).

Usually the game no longer loads it, and the decisions about its
collisions wait until the mod is on again. The game still loads it while
the manager has not deployed since the mod went off, or when a copy the
manager did not put there is still in the data directory and active.

loaded.description: Whether the game loads the plugin all the same.

mod.description: The switched-off mod that brings it.

oneOf.description: The faces of characters.
Textures, from loose files or archives.
Meshes and the textures they use.
Objects placed in the world.
One mod's plugin contained in the other.
Other files, such as scripts, sounds or animations.

UnrealPak.description:
One Unreal package a mod brought: the `.pak` file and the files that
belong to it (`.utoc`, `.ucas`).

bytes.description: The size of its files together, in bytes.

extensions.description:
The extensions of its files, in lower case, such as `pak`, `ucas`,
`utoc`.

path.description:
The package, below the directory the game is installed in, with
`/` between folders and as spelled on disk; without the extension.

provider.description: The mod its `.pak` file came from, if the mod manager knows.

WorldMap.description:
Where mods place objects in the world, cell by cell, and where objects
of two mods collide.

owners.description:
The mods (or plugins, where no mod is known) that place objects.
Cells refer to them by their position in this list.

spots.description: Every collision that a finding reports.

worlds.description:
The worldspaces in which mods place objects outside: first the one
with the most cells where several mods meet, then by objects.

oneOf.description: The game itself or its DLC.
Creation Club content the game lists as its own.
A mod.
